edges.note: The foreign key column stores the target row's Identity Field (primary key) value.
Join-table rows pair the two associated rows' Identity Field key values.

edges.cite: Fowler, PoEAA, 'Association Table Mapping' (When to Use)
edges.note: Both map object references to relational structure; pick by multiplicity (many-to-many needs a join table, else a FK column).
The owner writes dependent rows keyed by a foreign key back to the owner's table.
Both persist objects with no independent identity accessed only via an owner; own rows vs folded-in columns.
Two ways to store owner-only dependents: separate owner-managed rows vs one serialized blob column.
Map a small dependent value across owner columns vs serialize it into one LOB column.
Embedded Value maps a Value Object into the columns of its owner's table.
Rival schemes for mapping a class hierarchy: one table per concrete class vs one shared table with a discriminator.
One table per concrete leaf (fields duplicated) vs one table per class joined by shared key.
Inheritance Mappers organizes the mapper objects that drive a single-table inheritance scheme.
Mapper structure mirroring the hierarchy handles the per-class-table joins.
Each concrete-class mapper handles its own full-field table while inherited-field handling is delegated upward.
Metadata Mapping lets a Data Mapper read/generate mappings from metadata instead of hand-coding each mapper.
Query Object translates criteria over domain classes to SQL using the object-relational Metadata Mapping.
A buffer pool is a specialized cache of fixed-size disk pages mediating all reads/writes to disk.

edges.cite: Ramakrishnan & Gehrke, Database Management Systems, buffer management
edges.note: The buffer manager picks a victim frame via a replacement policy (LRU/clock) when no free frame exists.
The WAL rule forces a dirty page's log records to disk before that page may be flushed from the buffer pool.
Stampede protection guards the recompute-on-miss step of cache-aside so only one loader runs per key.
Singleflight/locking coalesces concurrent misses onto one loader invocation in a read-through cache.
Refresh-ahead reloads before expiry, avoiding the synchronized-expiry stampede that stampede-protection otherwise handles reactively.
Blocks are keyed by a cryptographic hash of their contents, making references self-verifying and writes idempotent.
Hash-keyed blocks referencing other blocks by hash form a Merkle DAG (e.g. Git, IPFS).
Immutable hash-keyed blocks are reclaimed by tracing/reference-counting unreferenced content (e.g. git gc).
Emulation journals variable records by appending to reserved pages and compacting via page swap, a log-structured scheme.
Rotating/swapping reserved pages spreads erase cycles so parameter storage does not wear out one block.
Both remap writes on erase-constrained flash; lightweight per-variable journaling vs a full block-device FTL.

edges.cite: Gal & Toledo 2005, ACM Computing Surveys, 'Algorithms and Data Structures for Flash Memories'
edges.note: The FTL's out-of-place remapping and block allocation implement wear leveling as part of presenting a rewritable device.
Out-of-place append/remap writes are what let wear leveling distribute erases evenly across blocks.
Resolving a foreign key checks the Identity Map first so the referenced object is materialized only once.
The Identity Map is keyed by the object's Identity Field so each row maps to one in-memory object.
Inline caching caches dynamic-dispatch lookup results per call site, a specialized cache of method/property resolution.

edges.cite: Holzle, Chambers & Ungar 1991, ECOOP, 'Optimizing Dynamically-Typed OO Languages with Polymorphic Inline Caches'
edges.note: The cached call-site guard checks the receiver's hidden class/map before the direct jump.
Megamorphic sites or invalidated assumptions on cached lookups trigger JIT deoptimization back to the interpreter.
Both trade space to avoid recomputation: precompute the whole table up front vs cache results lazily on demand.
Eager full precomputation with no misses/eviction vs an on-demand cache under an invalidation policy.
Sequential readahead loads pages into the buffer pool before the query requests them, overlapping I/O with work.
Populate the cache anticipatorily before requests vs lazily load on the first miss.
Refresh-ahead is temporal prefetch: it reloads an entry proactively just before its expiry.
Active Record is a Row Data Gateway enriched with domain/business logic on the wrapped row.
One gateway instance per row vs one gateway for all rows of a table; chosen by granularity.
A Table Data Gateway's finders return query results as a Record Set.
A Data Mapper can reach the database through Table Data Gateways rather than issuing SQL directly.
A Data Mapper consults an Identity Map to avoid loading the same row into two objects.
On commit, the Unit of Work drives the appropriate Data Mappers to insert/update/delete registered objects.
A Repository's collection-like interface is typically implemented on top of a Data Mapper layer.
Periodic snapshots accelerate rebuilding in-memory state so replay need not start from the beginning of the event log.
Batching several transactions' event-log records into one synchronous flush amortizes fsync cost for the durability log.
Group commit coalesces multiple committing transactions' WAL records into a single synchronous log flush.
A checkpoint flushes dirty pages out of the buffer pool and records how far recovery must scan the log.
A background cleaner compacts segments, copying still-live records out to reclaim space from overwritten data.
Log-as-storage (append is the data) vs log-then-update-in-place, where the log only aids recovery of a mutable store.
An LSM-tree applies the log-structured, append-and-compact principle to an ordered on-disk index.
Deletes in an LSM-tree are written as tombstone markers that shadow older values until compaction removes them.
Compaction is what actually purges tombstoned data after the grace period, reclaiming the shadowed records.
In append-only/log-structured stores a delete cannot overwrite in place, so it is recorded as a tombstone write.
On writes, synchronously propagate to the store before ack vs ack immediately and propagate asynchronously.
Cache products commonly pair a read-through loader with a write-through writer for a fully cache-managed store.
On a miss the application loads and populates the cache vs the cache itself loads via a pluggable loader.
Cached misses are held under their own, usually shorter, TTL so repeated failures are answered from cache.
Shadow paging is copy-on-write applied to page tables: modify a copied page then atomically swap the root, never overwriting in place.
A CoW B-tree copies each modified node up to a new root and swaps it in atomically - shadow paging applied to a B-tree.
An Identity Map is a session cache of loaded rows keyed by id, serving repeat lookups from memory rather than re-querying.
